text:
mike: Heads up — we're seeing intermittent failures resolving the interface endpoint for metrics.redwood-internal in us-west-2 when queries flow through our custom DNS forwarder (coredns on the DNS fleet). Direct host resolution from a jumpbox works fine.

sara: can you paste the dig output? is it NXDOMAIN or returns a public ip? any consistent pattern by AZ? :eyes:

mike: NXDOMAIN from pods in one EKS nodegroup, but from a bastion (same VPC) dig returns the private vpce DNS name -> 10.1.5.23 (ENI). Example:

```
; pod (via coredns -> forwarder)
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> metrics.redwood-internal.vpce.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;metrics.redwood-internal.vpce.us-west-2.amazonaws.com. IN A

; bastion (direct to AmazonProvidedDNS)
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> metrics.redwood-internal.vpce.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 54321
;; ANSWER SECTION:
metrics.redwood-internal.vpce.us-west-2.amazonaws.com. 60 IN A 10.1.5.23
```

charlie: interesting. sounds like the forwarder isn't forwarding the private hosted zone queries to the VPC resolver correctly. are we forwarding to the VPC resolver (.2) or to Route53 resolver endpoints?

mike: we forward unknown zones to the central DNS fleet which then either resolves or forwards to the VPC resolver IP (.2). I checked coredns, it forwards to 172.31.10.5 (central) which should forward to .2.

sara: two quick checks: 
1) confirm the VPC's DHCP options are AmazonProvidedDNS and that the pods end up using cluster DNS as expected (check /etc/resolv.conf in pod).
2) confirm the Route53 Resolver rules and associations — if the central DNS is using outbound endpoints it needs a rule for the private zone or to forward straight to the VPC .2 address.

anna: also check the interface endpoint setting "Enable private DNS" — if that was toggled recently the private hosted zone name could have been recreated in a different account/zone. we had a similar surprise when a cross-account endpoint was re-created.

mike: /etc/resolv.conf from a failing pod: 

```
search default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local us-west-2.compute.internal
nameserver 10.100.0.10  # kube-proxy/coredns
options ndots:5
```

so it hits coredns first. coredns forwards to 172.31.10.5 which is our central forwarder.

infra-bot: [ep-usw2-metrics] interface endpoint eni: eni-0a1b2c3d status=available az=us-west-2b privateDnsEnabled=true securityGroups=[sg-0ffeed11]

charlie: what's the central forwarder's config for the vpce.* zone? If it's doing recursion itself but not forwarding to the VPC resolver, Route53 private hosted zones won't be visible. You need to either: 
- forward the exact zone (vpce.us-west-2.amazonaws.com or the service FQDN) to the VPC .2; or 
- configure a Route53 Resolver outbound endpoint + forwarding rule that points at the VPC.

mike: central forwarder currently has a stub zone for "vpce.us-west-2.amazonaws.com" pointing to 10.0.0.2 (an old resolver that was decommissioned). Oops.

sara: that would explain NXDOMAIN. change the stub to forward to the VPC .2 (the AmazonProvidedDNS) or the VPC resolver IP in each VPC where endpoints live. If you're centralizing, prefer Route53 Resolver outbound endpoints and rules — more resilient across AZs.

mike: making the change now. will replace stub -> 10.0.0.2 with forwarder -> VPC .2 via per-vpc RFC1918 route/peering path.

deploy-bot: rolling update to dns-forwarder fleet started (5 pods at a time) by mike — changelist: swap stub target for vpce.* -> 10.0.0.2 to per-VPC .2 forwarding and add zone fallback.

mike: after the change, dig from the pod shows NOERROR and correct ENI IP. :tada:

```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> metrics.redwood-internal.vpce.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 67890
;; ANSWER SECTION:
metrics.redwood-internal.vpce.us-west-2.amazonaws.com. 60 IN A 10.1.5.23
```

sara: nice. long-term we should: 
- add automated tests for private DNS resolution across VPCs when updating stub zones
- document that central DNS must forward vpce/private hosted zones to the VPC resolver or use Route53 Resolver endpoints
- add monitoring alert for sudden NXDOMAIN rate spikes for any vpce.* name

charlie: also double-check SGs on the interface endpoint — we saw timeouts where the SG allowed 443 but the ENI source ip changed due to NAT from the forwarder fleet and the SG was only allowing subnet CIDR. recommend allowing the forwarder fleet SG explicitly.

mike: good call — I opened a follow-up ticket to widen the SG to allow the forwarder SG id.

anna: thanks for the quick turnaround. tagging infra oncall. :wave:

infra-bot: oncall assigned: anna

mike: closing the thread — will follow up with a runbook PR that includes the stub/forward rule guidance, and a postmortem note for the DNS fleet change that reintroduced the old resolver IP.

sara: cheers! :thumbsup:
